ca-sos-2026-weber-shirley.name: Shirley N. Weber
ca-sos-2026-weber-shirley.bio: California Secretary of State since 2021; former State Assemblymember and San Diego State University professor who helped found its Africana Studies Department.

positions.stance: Pledges to fix delayed financial filings in the Secretary of State's office, enforce rules equally, and be "fair and principled."
Supports an aggressive outreach campaign statewide urging Californians to register and vote, including high school and college students.
Committed to working with local elections officials "to strengthen, protect, and expand access to the ballot."
Wants to improve transparency in elections, lobbyist registration, and campaign finance systems so Californians can make informed decisions.
Committed to monitoring and upgrading the office's cybersecurity policies to protect elections from attempts to undermine democratic processes.

ca-sos-2026-wagner-donald.name: Donald P. (Don) Wagner
ca-sos-2026-wagner-donald.bio: Former Orange County Supervisor and board chairman, former Mayor of Irvine, former California State Assemblymember, and business lawyer.

positions.stance: Running to make sure "only eligible voters cast ballots."
Wants elections that are "secure, efficient, accurate, and accessible" to every eligible voter.
Wants the Secretary of State's business division to be "small-business friendly."
"Fully supports the Voter ID Initiative on the ballot in November."

ca-controller-2026-cohen-malia.name: Malia M. Cohen
ca-controller-2026-cohen-malia.bio: California State Controller; former member of the State Board of Equalization and former President of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors.

positions.stance: Working to expand housing availability at all income levels, incentivize affordable housing development, and assist first-time homebuyers.
Pledges to be "a fearless advocate for protecting retirement security" while keeping pension systems on sound fiscal footing.
Will focus on job creation and job training, prioritizing communities of color and low-income communities that have endured long-term disinvestment.
Will fight to expand health care access, lower costs, and demand greater accountability around prescription drug prices.
Says reproductive health care "is under attack" and pledges to "be a champion for reproductive access for all."

ca-controller-2026-morgan-herb.name: Herb W Morgan
ca-controller-2026-morgan-herb.bio: Investment professional who founded Efficient Market Advisors and later served as a chief investment officer; former chair of the San Diego City Employees' Retirement System board.

positions.stance: Wants real-time fiscal oversight so Californians know exactly how the state budget is spent "without delay, red tape, or political spin."
Proposes an open-ledger, blockchain-based public finance platform publishing every state agency ledger online in real time.
Plans risk-based, outcome-based audits of high-dollar programs while they operate, to stop waste, fraud, and abuse before it occurs.
Wants to give journalists, watchdogs, academics, and citizens direct access to state financial data.

ca-treas-2026-kounalakis-eleni.name: Eleni Kounalakis
ca-treas-2026-kounalakis-eleni.bio: Lieutenant Governor of California; former U.S. Ambassador to Hungary and former president of the housing development firm AKT Development.

ca-treas-2026-hawks-jennifer.name: Jennifer Hawks
ca-treas-2026-hawks-jennifer.bio: Retired business executive and budget-and-operations leader.

positions.stance: Would direct a comprehensive review of the Treasurer's Office divisions, controls, contracts, consultants and fees, then publish findings and corrective actions.
Would review the Pooled Money Investment Account holding by holding and make its reporting easier for taxpayers to scrutinize.
Would put California's full debt picture, including outstanding and authorized-but-unissued bonds and debt service, on one public dashboard.
Would press for searchable disclosure of housing project costs, developers, financing, tax credits, bond allocations, and repeat recipients.
Would bring investments, bond transactions, board actions, contracts and major financing decisions into one searchable location.

ca-ag-2026-bonta-rob.name: Rob Bonta
ca-ag-2026-bonta-rob.bio: California Attorney General; former State Assemblymember and Alameda City Council member.

positions.stance: Defending California's gun safety laws, including the assault weapons ban, and expanding gang-violence interruption programs and gun violence restraining orders.
Will strongly enforce California's civil rights code, "fight for racial justice and equity," and take on the forces of hate.
Taking on transnational criminal organizations trafficking guns, drugs and people, and expanding support programs for crime victims.
Believes "health care is a human right"; defending Obamacare and California's reproductive health care laws from legal attacks.
Believes the justice system should be safer, fairer, "free from bias," and more accountable to the people it serves.

ca-ag-2026-gates-michael.name: Michael E. Gates
ca-ag-2026-gates-michael.bio: Former Huntington Beach City Attorney and former Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the U.S. Department of Justice Civil Rights Division.

positions.stance: Will make public safety his top priority and make full statewide implementation of Proposition 36 his highest priority after taking office.
Believes local governments, not Sacramento, should make land-use and housing decisions; will push back against state mandates overriding local plans.
Will defend officers sued for doing their jobs and ensure police have the backing and resources needed to keep communities safe.
Will investigate and prosecute fraud at every level and demand full transparency with public reporting and independent audits.
Will enforce Title IX statewide, keep "boys out of girls' sports," and defend parents' rights to be informed about their children's education.
Leading the fight against insurers that "stall claims and refuse to compensate wildfire victims."
Says Californians deserve timely, fair treatment from insurers after a disaster; refuses insurance industry campaign contributions.
Will make it a top priority to modernize the Department of Insurance and make it more transparent and accountable.

ca-ins-2026-kim-jane.name: Jane Kim
ca-ins-2026-kim-jane.bio: Civil rights attorney, consumer advocate, legislator and organizer; former elected San Francisco Supervisor.

positions.stance: Will "stop insurance companies from jacking up rates, price gouging, and denying valid claims."
Says she has never taken money from insurance companies or their PACs, and refuses all corporate PAC money.
Will fight for Natural Disaster Insurance for All, fix the FAIR Plan, expand low-cost auto insurance, and invest in safer homes and communities.
Will enforce minimum coverage standards, create a statewide coverage calculator, and end price discrimination for auto insurance.
Will penalize claim delays, make insurers pay disaster survivors immediately, and create a public insurer performance dashboard.

tx-ag-2026-middleton-mayes.name: Mayes Middleton
tx-ag-2026-middleton-mayes.bio: Texas State Senator for District 11, former two-term Texas House member, attorney, and President of Middleton Oil Company.

positions.stance: Would sue to stop "sanctuary cities" and aggressively enforce President Trump's border security agenda and deportation orders.
Would "uphold pro-life laws" and stop efforts to "confuse our children with gender ideology."
Supports zero-tolerance policies for violent crime, stronger bonds for dangerous offenders, and reining in district attorneys who refuse to enforce the law.
Would "stop men from invading women's private spaces" and keep biological males from competing against females in sports.
Would ensure only legally qualified U.S. citizens vote in Texas elections and enforce Texas' voter ID laws.

tx-ag-2026-johnson-nathan.name: Nathan Johnson
tx-ag-2026-johnson-nathan.bio: Texas State Senator, litigator and mediator.

positions.stance: Would use the office to defend and restore individual rights and freedoms, and join other Democratic AGs in suing to block illegal Trump administration actions.
Will enforce Texas consumer protection and competition laws against price gouging, consumer scams, and unfair competition.
Would focus the office on core duties like child support, legal opinions, infrastructure finance, and government transparency, staffed by people who care.
Pledges to be an independent Attorney General who investigates and prosecutes officials "irrespective of political party."
Would work with district attorneys to keep Texans and their property safe, rather than taking an antagonistic approach to them.

tx-comptroller-2026-huffines-don.name: Don Huffines
tx-comptroller-2026-huffines-don.bio: Texas Comptroller; former Texas State Senator, founder of the Huffines Liberty Foundation, and co-founder of the real estate firm Huffines Communities.

positions.stance: Believes "the money belongs to the people, not the government"; will expose corruption and fight to jail those who steal taxpayer dollars.
Will conduct forensic audits across local governments and state agencies so that "no one in government will feel safe from a surprise audit."
Wants to run Texas lean with private-sector standards, focusing on how tax dollars are spent, not just how much is collected.
Will fight to slash property taxes and prioritize Texas companies for state contracts.
Will fight to eliminate "job-killing regulations" that hold Texas businesses back and drive up the cost of living.

tx-comptroller-2026-eckhardt-sarah.name: Sarah Eckhardt
tx-comptroller-2026-eckhardt-sarah.bio: Texas State Senator; former Travis County Judge, Travis County commissioner, and county prosecutor.

positions.stance: Says the comptroller "should be a watchdog for your money— not a lapdog for the rich and powerful."
Says the comptroller can protect schools and "audit the voucher scheme."
Says the comptroller can expose how much it costs when the state refuses Medicaid expansion.
Says the comptroller can "stop no-bid contracts to wealthy donors, and halt giveaways to AI data centers."
Running "to restore trust and accountability in government" so it works for the people who pay for it.

tx-land-2026-buckingham-dawn.name: Dawn Buckingham
tx-land-2026-buckingham-dawn.bio: Texas Land Commissioner since 2022; former Texas State Senator for District 24 and physician.

positions.stance: Made the General Land Office "the tip of the spear" for border defense, including offering GLO resources to detain and deport criminals here illegally.
Will continue "protecting funding for the school children of Texas" through state land revenue.
Oversees veteran nursing homes and cemeteries and chairs the Veterans Land Board, describing service to veterans as an honor.
Highlights delivering disaster recovery and flood mitigation funding to put families back in safe homes and help businesses stay afloat.
Works to protect Texas' energy dominance, saying "energy security is essential for national security," and opposes federal overreach.

tx-land-2026-flores-benjamin.name: Benjamin Flores
tx-land-2026-flores-benjamin.bio: Bay City council member and cybersecurity, risk management and compliance professional who runs a small heritage pig farm.

positions.stance: Would launch a 90-day review of the General Land Office's spending, contracts, and Harvey recovery funds, and publish findings and a corrective-action plan.
Would expand responsible energy leasing, including oil, gas, wind, solar and geothermal, to increase revenue for the Permanent School Fund.
Would prioritize moving outstanding Harvey recovery funds and payments forward and establish transparent reporting on recovery dollars.
Would review veterans' care providers, expand veterans' housing and loan assistance, and advocate for a full-service VA hospital in the Rio Grande Valley.
Would support living shorelines, wetland restoration, natural storm barriers, and improved disaster preparedness.

tx-agriculture-2026-sheets-nate.name: Nate Sheets
tx-agriculture-2026-sheets-nate.bio: U.S. Navy Reserve veteran and businessman who built a branded honey company from a single backyard beehive.

positions.stance: Will be "a tenacious ambassador for Texas First Trade" that creates jobs and increases the bottom line for farmers, ranchers, and producers.
Will help Texas producers "grow the cleanest food possible while growing their bottom line."
Will work with the legislature and Texas producers to serve students "the cleanest food possible" in school lunches.
Will work to bring jobs processing agricultural goods into finished products back to rural Texas.
Will work with the Legislature on strong state laws to investigate and punish agroterrorism by hostile nations like China.

tx-agriculture-2026-tucker-clayton.name: Clayton Tucker
tx-agriculture-2026-tucker-clayton.bio: Rancher on his family's ranch in Lampasas and Secretary of the Texas Farmers Union; former water and agriculture researcher and kindergarten teacher.

positions.stance: Supports the "Right to Repair all agricultural equipment."
Opposes AI data centers he says will bring "higher water and power bills, dry water wells, and no real jobs."
Says Texas is running out of water and opposes AI data centers, billionaires and Wall Street interests taking Texas' water.
"Fully supports the right for every farmer to raise hemp, and adults to consume hemp products, without undue interference."
Supports doing everything within reason to combat the New World Screwworm, including sterile flies and other proven methods.

tx-rrc-2026-french-bo.name: Bo French
tx-rrc-2026-french-bo.bio: Chairman of the Tarrant County Republican Party, rancher and mineral owner, former energy trader, and owner of security businesses in the Middle East.

positions.stance: Will push for policies that "expand oil and gas production, and make life more affordable in Texas."
Believes the Railroad Commission "should cut regulations rather than centralize its power in Austin."
Pledges to continue fighting what he calls "the Islamic invasion" of Texas from the Railroad Commission.
Will fight to end DEI-based contracting and return the Railroad Commission to merit-based decision-making.
Will push operator paperwork that pre-screens for organizations prohibited under the SB17 foreign-ownership ban, such as the Chinese Communist Party.

tx-rrc-2026-rosenthal-jon.name: Jon Rosenthal
tx-rrc-2026-rosenthal-jon.bio: Mechanical engineer with 25+ years of oilfield engineering experience and four-term Texas state legislator.

positions.stance: Top priority is lobbying for a dramatic RRC budget increase to plug orphan wells, hire more inspectors, and raise employee wages.
Supports weatherization requirements for critical gas infrastructure with deadlines, third-party audits, and fines, plus public reliability scorecards.
Would ban industry donations to Railroad Commissioners and publish commissioners' calendars, meetings, and recusals.
Would end routine flaring and venting, require modern leak detection, and strengthen groundwater safeguards and setback standards.
Would make "polluter pays" real by raising surety bonds, plugging orphan wells at scale, and restoring property.

fl-ag-2026-uthmeier-james.name: James Uthmeier
fl-ag-2026-uthmeier-james.bio: Florida Attorney General; former Chief of Staff to Governor Ron DeSantis and former senior advisor and counsel to the U.S. Secretary of Commerce.

fl-ag-2026-rodriguez-jose.name: Jose Javier Rodriguez
fl-ag-2026-rodriguez-jose.bio: Attorney, former Florida legislator in the House and Senate, and former U.S. Assistant Secretary of Labor.

positions.stance: Would "hold Big Tech and social media platforms accountable for hurting Florida's children."
Would aggressively prosecute criminal cartels, bust child exploitation networks, and stop lethal drugs, including opioids, from flooding the streets.
Would crack down on elder abuse, from marketing scams to guardianship abuse and abuse in assisted living facilities and nursing homes.
Would protect homeowners and renters by ending deed and title theft, contractor fraud, and predatory schemes through strict enforcement.
Would "provide resources to police and prosecutors to combat violent crime and gun violence."

fl-cfo-2026-ingoglia-blaise.name: Blaise Ingoglia
fl-cfo-2026-ingoglia-blaise.bio: Florida Chief Financial Officer and State Fire Marshal; former Florida State Senator.

positions.stance: "If you steal from Florida taxpayers, Blaise is coming for you"; highlights fraud arrests and audits exposing wasteful local government spending.
Says local governments "have a spending problem" and that property taxes can be cut while fully funding law enforcement and fire rescue.
Highlights fining and suing insurers and requiring qualified professionals, not solely AI, to review claim denials.
Says he "backs the blue," with his office's investigators arresting fraudsters and helping sheriffs close cases.
Highlights cancer coverage for firefighters, funding for fire departments, and workers' comp coverage for first responders with PTSD.

fl-cfo-2026-taddeo-annette.name: Annette Taddeo
fl-cfo-2026-taddeo-annette.bio: Small business owner who built the company LanguageSpeak; former Florida State Senator.

positions.stance: Would publicly grade every insurance company within her first 100 days on claim speed, denials, affiliate payments, and financial soundness.
Supports a bigger homestead exemption with a backstop for rural counties "so a tax cut doesn't come back as a higher tax rate."
Would match records and mail Floridians the unclaimed money the state owes them.
Would send strike teams to hard-hit communities within 3 to 5 days to help families push stalled and lowballed claims.
Would post every state contract in the public FACTS database and audit every no-bid deal.

fl-agr-2026-simpson-wilton.name: Wilton Simpson
fl-agr-2026-simpson-wilton.bio: Florida Commissioner of Agriculture, former Florida Senate President, and lifelong farmer and entrepreneur.

positions.stance: Says Florida farmers "will not be left behind" and highlights work protecting them from frivolous lawsuits.
Has fought vaccine mandates, protected parental choice, and ensured election integrity, saying Floridians "will not be cancelled by elitist socialists."
Has fought to ensure law enforcement officers "have the support and resources they need to do their jobs" and opposed defunding police.
"100% pro-life" and believes there is "a moral obligation to protect the unborn."
Has fought to keep Florida's businesses open, use taxpayers' money wisely, and keep Florida affordable.
Will fight to suspend the state gas tax and crack down on price gouging.
Supports a statewide moratorium and "will fight to block and ban data centers."
Will fight for family farms by protecting farmland from predatory developers.
Will fight to reinstate the Second Amendment rights of medical marijuana patients.
Will use his Cabinet position to expand Gov. DeSantis' ban on Flock cameras.

ny-comp-2026-dinapoli-thomas.name: Thomas P. DiNapoli
ny-comp-2026-dinapoli-thomas.bio: New York State Comptroller since 2007; former ten-term New York State Assemblymember.

positions.stance: Fighting back against "extremists who want to roll back women's rights, attack the foundations of our democracy and threaten New York's fiscal health."
Says "we need to protect the environment."
Supports "common sense gun safety reforms."
Supports policies "to make our streets, subways and homes safe."

ny-comp-2026-hernandez-joseph.name: Joseph Hernandez
ny-comp-2026-hernandez-joseph.bio: Entrepreneur and investor in biotechnology, healthcare and technology; Founder and Senior Managing Partner of Blue Water Venture Partners.

positions.stance: Believes "New York has a spending problem, not a revenue problem" and will challenge reckless spending.
Will aggressively audit state agencies, public authorities, and major spending initiatives to identify waste and failing programs.
Will aggressively use the comptroller's authority to challenge questionable contracts before taxpayer money is spent.
Will protect the integrity of the property tax cap and work to reduce financial pressures that drive local taxes higher.
Will make fighting fraud a central mission, including a dedicated Fraud Strike Task Force and stronger pre-payment monitoring.
Working to protect New Yorkers from gun violence, illegal firearms, and ghost guns through gun buybacks and enforcement.
Fighting for fair wages, good-paying jobs, and organized labor, and "laser-focused on keeping costs down for New Yorkers."
Champions laws cracking down on predatory lenders, abusive debt collectors, dishonest mortgage providers, and deed theft.
Has pursued individuals and corporations that tried to deprive New Yorkers of health care, including opioid makers and neglectful nursing homes.
Working to protect children's mental health online and protect seniors from scams and nursing home neglect.

ny-ag-2026-komatireddy-saritha.name: Saritha Komatireddy
ny-ag-2026-komatireddy-saritha.bio: Former federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of New York and former DEA Chief of Staff; law firm partner and Columbia Law School instructor.

positions.stance: "If New York isn't safe, nothing else matters"; pledges to focus on safety.
Pledges to "enforce the law by prosecuting crime."
Pledges to "take the homeless and the sick off the street humanely."
Pledges to "eliminate corruption and fraud."
